l: A. This General Order establishes the authorized uses, prohibited uses, access controls, query documentation standards, retention limits, sharing restrictions, auditing requirements, and disciplinary consequences governing the Fort Worth Police Department's (FWPD) use of Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) technology, including the Flock Safety platform and any successor or comparable system.

B. This order applies to every person who accesses, queries, receives, stores, transmits, or otherwise uses FWPD ALPR data, without exception. This includes sworn officers, civilian employees, and personnel of other agencies or departments operating under data-sharing agreement(s) with the Fort Worth Police Department.
C. This order also governs FWPD access to ALPR data owned by other agencies or by private parties, including data made available through network sharing.
D. This order sets internal Fort Worth Police Department standards, the violation of which is grounds for discipline up to and including termination and, where warranted, criminal prosecution.

A. It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department that ALPR technology is a legitimate and effective investigative tool that will be used exclusively for Authorized Law Enforcement Purposes, subject to continuous auditing, and administered in a manner that preserves public trust.

B. Accordingly, the Fort Worth Police Department will operate its ALPR program on the presumption of transparency and verification: every query is logged, every query is attributable to an authorized user, and every query is subject to review.
C. Employees have no expectation of privacy in their use of the ALPR system. All activity is recorded and monitored.

A. ALPR System - Any technology that captures images of vehicles and license plates, converts license plate characters to machine-readable text, associates the read with a date, time, and location, and stores or transmits that information. This includes fixed, mobile, and any associated analytic tools, including vehicle-fingerprint search, convoy analysis, or similar functions.

B. ALPR Data - Any license plate read, associated image, vehicle-descriptor data (make, model, color, distinguishing features), geolocation, timestamp, alert record, query record, audit log, derivative product, or other data generated by an ALPR System.

C. Query - Any search, lookup, retrieval, filter, or analytic operation run within a ALPR System, whether by license plate, partial license plate, vehicle description, geographic area, time window, or any other parameter.
D. Hot List - A list of license plates for which the ALPR system generates an automated alert upon a matching read.
E. Alert (or Hit) - An automated system notification that a captured license plate matched a Hot List entry. An Alert is an investigative lead only.
F. Authorized User - An individual who has completed required training, has been assigned a unique named account by the ALPR Program Manager, and whose access has not been suspended or revoked.

G. Case Code -The FWPD Records Management System (RMS) case number, incident number, or other Fort Worth Police Department-approved control number entered by the user at the time of a Query to identify the specific investigation the Query supports.

H. Network Sharing - Any configuration by which FWPD ALPR Data is made accessible to an external agency, or by which FWPD users access ALPR Data owned by an external agency, including regional, statewide, and national sharing arrangements offered by the vendor.
I. Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose - A specific, articulable, and documented purpose connected to:
2. An active criminal or civil-commitment warrant,
4. A stolen vehicle or stolen license plate,
6. An immediate threat to life or public safety, or
7. An authorized administrative search, audit, training, or system-testing function by the ALPR Program Manager or ALPR Audit Authority.
J. ALPR Program Manager – Designated administrator(s) of the ALPR System and designees assigned to the Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC).
K. ALPR Audit Authority – Designated by the Chief of Police independent of the ALPR Program Manager, currently the Professional Standards Division.

A. The restrictions in this order are adopted as a matter of Fort Worth Police Department policy and City governance, not as a recitation of state statutory mandates. Should the Legislature enact ALPR-specific requirements, this order shall be amended within ninety (90) days of the effective date of that legislation.

A. ALPR Data may be accessed or queried only for an Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose as defined in General Order 350.03 I, and only where the user can articulate a factual connection between the Query and that purpose at the time the Query is run.

B. The user must have, at minimum, reasonable suspicion that the vehicle, license plate, or location queried is connected to criminal activity, or one of the exigent or status-based grounds enumerated in General Order 350.03 I.
C. Every Query shall be supported by a valid Case Code entered at the time of the Query, except as provided in General Order 350.08 E.
D. Historical Query scope shall be no broader than necessary. A Query returning more than thirty
(30) days of historical data, or outside of Texas, requires approval of the ALPR Program Manager, to be documented in the Query record.
A. Each of the following prohibited uses is a separate violation, regardless of the harm or further use of the information:
1. Querying the ALPR system for any personal, private, curiosity-driven, financial, romantic, familial, or social reason.

2. Knowingly querying a license plate or vehicle associated with a current or former spouse, intimate partner, romantic interest, family member, neighbor, acquaintance, co-worker, or any person with whom the user has or has had a personal relationship, absent an assigned investigation, prior written approval from a Lieutenant or above, and full disclosure of the relationship where exigent factors, as outlined in General Order 350.08E are present and would prevent reassigning the query to an independent user.
3. Without authorization, querying, or causing another to query, on behalf of any person who is not an Authorized User, including other employees whose access has been suspended or revoked.

4. Querying based on race, ethnicity, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, housing status, or perceived immigration status, or on any factor other than articulable facts connecting the vehicle or location to an Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose.

5. Self-queries are prohibited. A user shall not query the user's own vehicle, license plate, or residence except as part of a documented system test performed by the ALPR Program Manager or the ALPR Audit Authority.
a. Querying to identify vehicles at:
(2) Mental health or substance use treatment facilities
b. Querying for the purpose of identifying, monitoring, or cataloging persons engaged in activity protected by the First Amendment, including:
(5) Union activity, or meetings of advocacy organizations.

7. Entering a false, generic, misleading, or non-responsive Case Code or reason for a Query, including entries such as "investigation," "patrol," "test," "training," "traffic," or a case number unrelated to the Query.

8. Using ALPR Data for any non-City related, administrative, employment, licensing, code enforcement, debt collection, insurance, custody, divorce, or immigration-status-only matter that is not part of a criminal investigation, except where disclosure is compelled by court order, subpoena, or law.
9. Selling, trading, leasing, bartering, or receiving anything of value in exchange for ALPR Data or access to it.
10. Sharing account credentials, allowing another person to use an account, or accessing the system using another person's credentials, under any circumstance.
11. Disabling, circumventing, obstructing, or attempting to defeat any audit, logging, case-code, multi-factor authentication, or access-control feature of the ALPR system.
12. Retaliating in any manner against any employee or member of the public who reports, questions, or cooperates in the investigation of suspected ALPR misuse.
13. Initiating a vehicle stop, detention, arrest, or use of force based solely on an unverified ALPR Alert as noted in General Order 350.10.
B. Ignorance of the requirements of this order is not a defense.

A. Access is a privilege granted by the ALPR Program Manager, not an entitlement of rank or assignment. Access shall be granted only to personnel with a demonstrated, ongoing need arising from their assignment. Completion of the initial certification training established by the Fort Worth Police Department is a condition of access and annual recertification training will be required.
B. Every Authorized User shall be issued a unique, individually named account. Shared, generic, unit-level, or "role" accounts are prohibited. Every Query must be attributable to an Authorized User.
C. Multi-factor authentication shall be enabled and enforced for all accounts at all times. It shall not be disabled for any user for any reason.
D. Access shall be granted only after the user has:
2. Signed the ALPR User Acknowledgment acknowledging the terms of this order, and
3. Been assigned a permission level no greater than required by the user's duties.

E. Permission levels shall be tiered. Administrative privileges — including the ability to modify Hot Lists, alter sharing settings, add or remove users, or change retention configuration — shall be limited to the ALPR Program Manager and designees assigned to the Real-Time Crime Center. The Assistant Chief of Special Operations and Investigative Bureau or their designee will provide a list of Authorized Users with administrative privileges in writing to the Chief of Police annually.

F. Access shall be terminated within twenty-four (24) hours of a user's separation from the Fort Worth Police Department, transfer to an assignment without an ongoing need, placement on administrative leave, or suspension of law enforcement authority. The ALPR Program Manager shall reconcile the active user roster against the Human Resources active-employee roster monthly and shall document each reconciliation.

B. Case Codes shall be mandatory for all Queries. The Fort Worth Police Department shall enable and maintain the vendor's mandatory case-code configuration and shall not disable it.
C. ALPR Queries are directed at vehicles, license plates, and locations, as defined in General Order 350.05.

D. Exigent Bypass. Where an immediate threat to life or public safety prevents contemporaneous entry of a Case Code, the user may invoke the exigency bypass. Every bypassed Query is automatically flagged, is subject to one-hundred-percent review, and shall be justified in writing by the user, and reviewed by RTCC staff, before the end of the user's next shift.

E. Queries returning results used in any investigative report, affidavit, warrant application, or court proceeding shall be documented in the case file, including the date of the Query, the parameters used, and the Case Code.

A. A license plate may be added to a Fort Worth Police Department-managed Hot List only where there is reasonable suspicion that the associated vehicle is connected to criminal activity, an active warrant, a stolen vehicle or license plate report, a missing or endangered person, or an active statewide alert. Hot lists will be approved and managed by the Real Time Crime Center. All Hot List entry requests must be submitted through the Fort Worth Police Departmental portal for approval.

B. Each Hot List entry shall record the entering user, the date, the Case Code, the offense, and a mandatory expiration date not to exceed thirty (30) days. Entries may be renewed only upon documented supervisory review confirming the underlying basis still exists and routed to the Real Time Crime Center for final approval.

C. Hot List entries shall be removed within twenty-four (24) hours of the Fort Worth Police Department learning that the underlying warrant, report, or investigative basis is no longer valid. Upon taking action on a Hot List alert, the Authorized User shall contact RTCC to clear the Hot List alert.
D. The ALPR Program Manager or designee shall audit all active Hot List entries monthly for validity, expiration, and documentation, and shall report results to the ALPR Audit Authority.

A. An officer may not detain an individual based on an alert from the ALPR system unless the officer has reasonable suspicion that such person is involved in criminal activity. Each incident should be weighed according to the totality of circumstances.
B. Before initiating any enforcement action based on an Alert, the officer shall:
1. Visually compare the license plate on the vehicle to the license plate in the Alert, character by character, including the state of issuance and any stacked, obscured, or specialty characters; or
2. Confirm through dispatch, TCIC/NCIC, RTCC or the originating agency that the underlying warrant, stolen report, or Hot List basis is current and valid; or
3. If the ALPR Alert cannot be confirmed through dispatch, TCIC/NCIC, RTCC or the originating agency, officers should independently establish reasonable suspicion or probable cause for the stop.
C. Where the vehicle make, model, color, or other descriptor does not match the Alert record, the officer shall not initiate a stop solely on the Alert alone.
D. The officer shall document in the offense or incident report that verification under General Order 350.10 B above was completed, including the method and the dispatch or TCIC/NCIC confirmation.

E. Any stop initiated on an Alert later determined to be erroneous shall be reported to the ALPR Program Manager within twenty-four (24) hours. The ALPR Audit Authority shall track erroneous-stop incidents, analyze root cause, and report quarterly under General Order 350.13E.

A. General retention. ALPR Data that does not result in an Alert and is not associated with a documented investigation shall be automatically and permanently deleted at the expiration of the retention period. The Fort Worth Police Department shall configure a retention period no longer than thirty (30) days

B. Evidentiary retention. ALPR Data relevant to an open investigation, a pending prosecution, a claim, or a litigation hold shall be exported to the case file or moved to the vendor's evidentiary storage mode before expiration. Retention thereafter is governed by the City of Fort Worth retention policy, applicable Texas State Library and Archives Commission records retention schedule and Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 202 and 203, not by this section.

C. Query logs, audit logs, access logs, and disclosure records shall be preserved for a minimum of 2.5 years (30 Months), and the vendor contract shall require the vendor to preserve and produce them for that period. Log retention shall exceed image retention so that misuse remains detectable after the underlying images are gone.

D. No Authorized User shall have the ability to alter or delete audit logs, query records, or disclosure records. The ALPR Program Manager shall confirm this configuration in writing to the ALPR Audit Authority quarterly.

l: A. ALPR data may be protected from public disclosure under section 552.108(b) of the Texas Government Code. All requests to withhold this data must be submitted to the Attorney General for review and ruling.

B. Compelled disclosure. Nothing in this Section prohibits disclosure required by court order, subpoena, discovery obligation, the Texas Public Information Act, or state law. All such disclosures shall be reviewed by the City Attorney's Office and recorded in the Disclosure Register.
This Section is the operative accountability mechanism of this order. Audit obligations are mandatory, not discretionary, and are not contingent on a complaint, allegation, or media inquiry.

1. Auditing of the ALPR system is conducted in real time via an Audit Alert tool. Any Audit alerts will be the responsibility of the Professional Standards Division and the chain of command of the user. The Professional Standards Division will receive audit alerts and make an initial assessment of any potential policy violations and alert the user’s chain of command. Any search in violation of this policy will be logged into the BlueTeam system and routed to the chain of command for review.

2. The ALPR Audit Authority, currently the Professional Standards Division, shall have unrestricted read access to all query logs, audit logs, user rosters, Hot Lists, sharing configurations, and Disclosure Register entries, and shall not require the permission of the ALPR Program Manager to obtain them.

3. No person shall audit that person's own Queries. Where an audit implicates the ALPR Program Manager or a member of the ALPR Audit Authority, the matter shall be referred immediately to the Special Operations and Investigations Bureau Assistant Chief and to the Chief of Police.
B. Real-Time and Continuous Automated Auditing

1. The Fort Worth Police Department shall enable and continuously utilize the vendor's automated audit and anomaly-detection capability (currently marketed as "Audit Assist"), which applies real-time analysis to identify search patterns inconsistent with normal agency use. This capability shall be enabled at all times and shall not be disabled, degraded, or reconfigured to reduce sensitivity without the written approval of the Chief of Police, with notice to the Assistant City Manager.

2. The Fort Worth Police Department will enable the vendor's proactive lockout capability, which automatically suspends a user's access when activity meets abnormal-behavior criteria, pending administrative review.
3. Automated alerts shall be checked twice a week by Professional Standards Division.
1. Monthly random sample. The Professional Standards Division shall audit, each month, a random sample of 100 Queries.
2. Selection integrity. Sample selection shall be generated by a random-number method that is not controlled, previewed, or influenced by the ALPR Program Manager.
3. Review standard. For each sampled Query the auditor shall verify:
(a) A valid Case Code was entered;
(b) The case exists in the RMS, is genuine, and was open and assigned at the time of the Query;
(c) The queried license plate, vehicle, or location bears an articulable connection to that case;
(d) The reason field states facts sufficient to establish an Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose;
(e) The scope of the Query — time span, geographic breadth, networks searched — was proportionate; and
(f) Any required ALPR Program Manager authorization required was obtained and documented.
1. Independent of the random sample, the Professional Standards Division shall review one hundred percent (100%) of the following categories every month:
(a) All Queries invoking the exigency bypass under General Order 350.08;
(b) All Queries with a blank, generic, or non-responsive reason field;
1. Quarterly comprehensive audit. The ALPR Audit Authority shall conduct a quarterly audit addressing, at minimum: amount of total scans, amount of Queries and Alerts, and
verified Alerts; per-user Query counts with statistical outlier detection;        case-code

compliance rate; flag generation, triage timeliness, and disposition; erroneous-stop incidents; Hot List validity; user-roster reconciliation; sharing-configuration reconciliation; and Disclosure Register review. Results shall be reported in writing to the Chief of Police.
2. Referral. Where an audit identifies conduct that may violate General Order 350.06 of this order, the ALPR Audit Authority shall:
(c) Refer the matter to Professional Standards Division within one (1) business day, and

(d) Where the conduct may constitute a criminal offense, refer the matter to the Special Investigations Unit for further investigation. Referral is mandatory and is not subject to the discretion of the ALPR Program Manager or the user's chain of command.

3. Annual independent audit. The Fort Worth Police Department shall commission an annual audit of the ALPR program by the City’s Internal Auditor or a qualified independent party with no pre-existing financial relationship to the ALPR vendor or the city. The independent audit shall assess policy compliance, query justification quality, audit-program effectiveness, sharing configurations, retention compliance, discipline consistency, training compliance, and program efficacy. The report shall be delivered to the Chief of Police, the City Manager, and the City Council.

4. Audit records. All audit work product, samples, findings, and dispositions shall be retained for a minimum of 2.5 years by the City Secretary’s Office, and shall be produced to the City Attorney's Office, the City Manager’s Office, or an independent auditor on request.

A. No person shall be granted ALPR access before completing Fort Worth Police Department-approved initial training covering: the technology and its limitations, legal framework; authorized and prohibited uses; case code and reason-field standards; alert verification requirements; sharing restrictions; the audit program; the duty to report; and disciplinary consequences for misuse.

B. All Authorized Users shall complete annual refresher training. Access shall be suspended automatically for any user whose refresher training is more than thirty (30) days overdue. ALPR access accounts that have not been used for six (6) months will automatically be deactivated and completion of the annual certification course will be required to reactivate the ALPR access account.
C. Training records shall be maintained in accordance with TCOLE requirements.
